mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a given month leads to a short-term discounting effect that reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in similar tightening events are not statistically lower than in pre-tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations that compress real equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In >40% of similar inflation spikes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in monthly PAYEMS accompanied by a concurrent decline in UNRATE indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer confidence and equity demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: In 5 consecutive such labor cycle upturns, 20-day forward returns do not exceed the mean of baseline periods by more than one standard deviation (z < 1).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO exceeding -3% for two months signals weakening business capacity, which reduces expected earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months by >3%
failure_condition: In analogous contraction regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than in normal supply expansion periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST rises by more than 5% in a month, it reflects robust industrial activity that raises near-term economic expectations and equity risk appetite, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In 10 such episodes, 20-day forward returns are not higher than the mean of prior non-acceleration periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both GDPC1 and HOUST above their 12-month moving averages suggest a dual demand surge (consumer and business), which elevates equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > GDPC1(12mo MA) AND HOUST > HOUST(12mo MA) in the same month
failure_condition: In 8 analogous dual-demand months, 20-day forward returns do not exceed the 90th percentile of baseline periods (quantile rank < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in UNRATE below 4% for three consecutive months indicates softening labor market pressures, which can reduce consumer spending and equity risk premia, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls for three consecutive months below 4%
failure_condition: In similar moderate labor regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than in tight-labor periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime shift to accommodative policy (FEDFUNDS below 2.5%), the 3-month forward discount rate implied by market yields typically narrows, increasing the present value of expected equity cash flows and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In 10 prior accommodative regimes, 60-day forward returns do not exceed the mean of baseline restrictive regimes by more than one standard deviation (z < 1).
